label: consistent

said.text: Congress has the power to declare war. … Congress must reclaim its rightful place as the first branch of government—exactly as the Founders intended.

did.text: Voted Yes on H.Con.Res. 108, directing the President pursuant to the War Powers Resolution to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities in Lebanon. Failed 189–235.

whyNote: The March statement concerned U.S. military action in Iran, not Lebanon; it is quoted here for its general position that decisions on hostilities require congressional authorization. In June, Rep. Torres voted yes on a war powers resolution concerning Lebanon.
editorNote: Held: the statement concerns Iran (Mar) and is spliced across two sentences; too indirect to pair with the June Lebanon vote even with disclosure.
